note: Contrarian Shark, angle **steel-man-the-premise**. Premises taken at their strongest reading, then attacked where that reading still fails the North Star. Findings limited to issues that survive the inclusion test.

findings.topic: E1 gutting positive NS capabilities without S1 trip
findings.section: The exit register; Phase 6 — S1 Validation Session
findings.criterion: John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach
findings.message: Steel-man the plan’s own acceptance system: exits are enumerated, signed, conjunction-scored; S1 alone may declare the North Star met; E6 is closed for the four violation classes. Even then the premise fails. The North Star is not only “no dead/silent/mislabelled/binary lies” — it is a **positive capability claim**: John **can** Doctor-diagnose and session-attach. E1 (`not available on this build`) is a legal signed exit that ships a named disabled control. S1’s build-blocking set is only the four **violation** classes (dead control, silent zero, mislabelled empty, raw-binary preview). A correctly labelled “Diagnose unavailable — reason” is **not** a dead control and does not trip E6’s closed complement. So the strongest reading still allows: signed E1 on Diagnose and/or attach → criteria closed with exits → free-traversal meets no four-class defect → S1 authorized to declare the North Star met while John **cannot** perform the actions the North Star names. The exit register does not close the escape chain on the positive half of the North Star; it formalizes gutting it. Fix required: either E1 on any control named in the North Star’s positive clause is an automatic NS-unmet (and S1 may not declare met), or E1 on those controls is forbidden without a North-Star amendment, not merely an exit row.

findings.section: Phase 2 — Capability Inventory & Rollup Evidence Gate; Phase 4 — Surface Waves
findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control; every surface … either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: Steel-man the plan’s anti-dead-control premise: EXISTS only with a real transcript (curl/CLI/REPL), STUB always “build it,” wave acceptance requires a schema-validated end-to-end trace with `capability_call` and `external_observable`. The foundational premise still equates **“capability can be invoked out-of-band”** with **“the user-facing control is alive.”** A dead control in product terms is almost always a **path** failure: button bound to a no-op, wrong handler, swallowed promise, feature flag off in UI only, or a STUB that the REPL path never hits. A pasted CLI transcript of the “real” backend function does not observe the click path; the inventory can stamp EXISTS while the control remains dead. The later UI trace is supposed to catch that — but wave scoping, “wire it” classification, and dependency order are all driven by the inventory verdict **before** that trace exists. The steel-man therefore schedules wiring and GREEN-prep against the wrong evidence object. Required: EXISTS (or “wire it”) must be earned by a **control-path** transcript (same interaction the user performs), not by a side-channel invocation; side-channel proof may support “backend present” but must not authorize “wire it.”

findings.topic: single restart control vs per-context restarts
findings.section: Success criteria (SC-1 vs SC-5); Phase 4 — Restart waves
findings.criterion: stop, and restart real Anchor work … without meeting a dead control
findings.message: Steel-man SC-5 as intentional de-duplication inside each restart context, with unification explicitly out of scope. The plan still opens SC-1 with elimination of dead controls for “**a single restart control** — work or not shown,” then SC-5 requires “**exactly one restart control per enumerated restart context**” and multiple scope names (run/session/engine/workbench). Those are not the same premise. Under the stronger SC-5 reading, John can still meet several restart affordances across contexts; under the stronger SC-1 reading, more than one restart control anywhere is a criterion failure. The plan never reconciles which claim the North Star’s “restart” is evaluated against. A build can GREEN SC-5 by cleaning each context while SC-1’s “single restart control” is quietly reinterpreted — or fail SC-1 while claiming multi-context honesty. That is not a wording NIT: dead-control elimination for restart is unfalsifiable until the unit of “control” is one object. Required: one locked definition — global single control **or** per-context uniqueness — and SC-1 rewritten to match SC-5 (or the reverse) so “restart works or is not shown” has a single testable referent.

findings.topic: external_observable unfit for pure diagnose/read paths
findings.section: Phase 3 — End-to-end trace artifact schema; Phase 4 — Doctor wave
findings.criterion: Doctor diagnose … either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: Steel-man the trace schema: a dead control is one that reaches a handler and makes no capability call / leaves no external side effect. For attach/stop/restart that is often right. For **Doctor diagnose** and several health surfaces, correct success is often **report-only**: credential_present, auth_round_trip result, or “no diagnostic available” — no row written, no file, no child process, no mandatory network write. Forcing a non-null `external_observable` (row/file/pid/request) either (a) invents fake side effects to satisfy the validator (theater the plan forbids), or (b) marks honest diagnose traces `invalid`/`dead`. The steel-man of “one universal liveness proof” therefore breaks the Doctor criterion it claims to protect. Required: per-control observable classes in the schema — including **read/report observables** (typed response body + depth label + forced-failure distinguishability) as first-class alternatives to mutation side effects — with the Doctor wave naming which class applies **before** work starts.

findings.topic: one blank verification task cannot falsify multi-surface NS
findings.section: Phase 1 — Ground Truth (verification task triple); Phase 6 — S1
findings.criterion: open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach; Steward conversational proof is S1
findings.message: Steel-man the triple as the shared referent that makes every criterion and S1 falsifiable: all fields filled, all three engines, duration long enough to stop mid-run and restart, every wave and S1 cite TASK-NAME. Even filled, **one** task is asked to be simultaneously long-running (stop/restart meaningful), multi-engine (Claude/Gemini/Grok), attach-bearing, and Doctor-bearing. Those are different runtime shapes; a single “exact command” rarely produces all of them without becoming an unspecified kitchen-sink whose failure modes cannot be attributed. Until the plan admits a **task set** (or explicit multi-step scenario with named sub-referents), “real Anchor work” remains one label over incompatible exercises — and S1 free-traversal against “the Phase 0 triple” can miss attach or Doctor while still “running the named task.” The blanks in the draft also leave the Master Plan under review **currently** unfalsifiable; Wave-1 hard-block does not make the draft’s claims evaluable **now**. Required: either a minimal task **set** covering open/run/stop/restart, attach, and per-engine diagnose, or an explicit multi-phase scenario protocol with separate acceptance hooks — not one underspecified command line.

findings.topic: E4 tripwire undefined so instrumentation budget is aspirational
findings.criterion: John can open, run, stop, and restart … (surfaces actually built, not only harnessed)
findings.message: Steel-man the budget: load-bearing vs discretionary named; E4 pre-defined with lighter forms; Phase 0–2 output capped; likelihood #2 mitigated by E4. The premise still has **no operational tripwire**. “If Phases 0–2 have not completed by the point at which surface work must start” never defines that point (calendar, wave-count, hours, or “first surface wave may not slip past N”). Without a numeric or calendar gate, E4 is only taken when someone notices overrun — the exact failure mode the section says is more likely than lying controls. Load-bearing items alone (vocabulary, tri-state harness, trace schema, cost_state, zero-inference lint) can still consume the effort. The North Star fails equally if Diagnose remains dead under an excellent harness. Required: a pre-committed surface-start deadline or max Phase 0–2 wave/time budget that **forces** the E4 register row, not a judgment call mid-stall.

findings.section: Phase 2 — three-way reclassification; Deferred build-it waves
findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control (and Doctor/attach work end-to-end)
findings.message: Steel-man the anti-escape rule: STUB may never become E1; STUB is always “build it” or renegotiation — correctly blocks laundering dead controls into labels. The premise of the effort is still **defect-remediation on v1.2**, not open-ended backend construction. If inventory returns multiple STUBs on NS-named controls, the plan obligates new full capability builds (own waves, own acceptance, dependency order) with no cap, no sizing gate, and no pre-agreed “renegotiate North Star vs absorb N build-it waves” threshold. Until those waves GREEN, the user-facing STUB **is** the dead control the North Star forbids. Steel-man therefore creates either unbounded scope explosion or a long window where dead controls remain live in the product while “build it” queues. Required: inventory-driven **scope freeze** with John after Phase 1 — explicit choose per STUB: fund build-it in this effort (sized), amend North Star, or HALT — not an automatic infinite “build it, always” that the defect-remediation premise cannot carry.

findings.topic: cost honesty met by permanent unmeasured / no dollars
findings.section: Success criteria SC-3; Phase 0 rollup spot-check; Phase 3 cost_state migration; Phase 4 usage wave
findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars; every surface that claims … usage … works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: Steel-man the cost rules: E2 banned for dollars; wrong spot-check → `measurement_failed`; labelling only from `cost_state`; existing rows default `unmeasured`; no `$0.00` as fact. That prevents fabrication. It also permits a GREEN “cost honesty” outcome where **no surface ever shows a real dollar figure** — historical rows unmeasured, backfill deferred, measurement_failed or unmeasured as the steady state — while SC-3’s practical-usefulness clause (real numbers within 60s after the named task) is satisfied only for usage/time or waived via pending/E5. “Cost never fabricates dollars” is then met by **never claiming cost**, which is weaker than a surface that “claims … usage” honesty implies for cost chrome that still occupies UI. The steel-man of non-fabrication becomes empty chrome that looks like a cost surface. Required: define when a cost surface must show `measured` dollars vs when the control must be **not shown** (SC-1 style) rather than left up as perpetual unmeasured/failed; perpetual unmeasured on a surface that still claims “cost” is a mislabelled empty/unknown risk relative to user expectation.

findings.topic: shared-schema writes vs nothing ships to v1.1.x
findings.section: Phase 1 shared-artifact ledger; Phase 3 cost_state migration
findings.criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
findings.message: Steel-man the isolation design: per-artifact yes/no, named mechanism (separate DB, additive migration behind flag default off, versioned assets), collaborator smoke after shared writes. “Ships” is never defined. An additive nullable `cost_state` column on a **shared** database is still a schema change collaborators’ stack loads, migrates, or fails on — even if the feature flag defaults off and UI is v1.2-only. Flag-off does not mean “nothing shipped” if migration runs on shared storage. The ledger can record “isolation = feature flag” while the North Star’s collaborator clause is already violated at the schema layer. Required: define “ships” (binary deploy, schema migrate, shared config, package version) and ban shared-schema mutations unless the ledger row names a mechanism that leaves v1.1.x **byte-identical** on disk/DB (e.g. separate DB or non-migrating side store) — flag-default-off alone is insufficient.

findings.topic: criteria-met status language dilutes NS pending
findings.section: Exit register status string; standing rules; Phase 6
findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build
findings.message: Steel-man the reporting rule: unqualified “ten criteria met” only with zero exits; otherwise “ten criteria met with N signed exits …; North Star pending S1.” The plan correctly withholds NS-met from automation. It still authorizes a triumphant **criteria-met** prefix as terminal build status before S1. That is not a silent NS claim, but it is a **proxy-success claim** that the plan’s own prose says is how teams stop early. Steel-man of S1-as-sole-NS-gate is weakened whenever status leads with “ten criteria met.” Prefer terminal status that cannot be skimmed as done — e.g. `build proxy complete; North Star pending S1` with no “criteria met” phrasing until S1 returns — so the steward clause cannot be socially satisfied by the proxy line alone.

findings.topic: first capture of inventory evidence still John-bound
findings.criterion: surfaces work end-to-end on John’s real v1.2 environment (implied by “on branch v1.2” and transcript-from-real-environment rules)
findings.message: Steel-man capture-once-replay-many: after first capture, harness does not need John live; E5 covers non-hard-blocker waits. Live-John list is “exhaustive” and omits the **first** inventory/rollup transcript capture on his real environment — yet Phase 1 rules require those transcripts from his v1.2. Alternate producers are promised “where one exists” but not named for capability transcripts. If John is the bottleneck (likelihood #1), Phase 1 stalls without E5 on the inventory itself, or someone captures against a non-John environment and launders it as “John’s real v1.2.” Required: name alternate producer or E5/HALT policy for **initial** Phase 1 evidence capture explicitly; do not list live-John items as exhaustive while the phase’s load-bearing inputs are missing from the list.
